t: Turkey's invasion of Cyprus on 20 July 1974, after a Greek-backed coup there, brought down the junta; Konstantinos Karamanlis returned, the first multiparty elections since 1964 were held, and a 1975 referendum rejected the monarchy.

Greece became the tenth member of the European Communities in 1981, adopted the euro in January 2001 and hosted the 2004 Summer Olympic Games in Athens; New Democracy and PASOK alternated in power for four decades.

The debt crisis from 2010 brought bailouts of 110 billion and 130 billion euros, a 25% fall in GDP between 2009 and 2015 and the emigration of 350,000 to 450,000 people before the bailouts ended in 2018.
dyk: The Greek merchant fleet, the largest in the world at 18% of global capacity and first in tankers and dry bulk carriers, was built after the Second World War from surplus ships sold off by the United States government.
ev: Turkey invades Cyprus on 20 July after a Greek-backed coup; the junta collapses, Konstantinos Karamanlis returns and the first multiparty elections since 1964 are held.
A democratic and republican constitution is promulgated after a referendum chooses not to restore the monarchy.
Greece becomes the tenth member of the European Communities; Andreas Papandreou's PASOK comes to power.
The euro replaces the drachma in January.
Athens hosts the Summer Olympic Games.
A 110 billion euro rescue package from the eurozone and the IMF averts default; harsh austerity follows.
The bailouts end; Alexis Tsipras and Zoran Zaev sign the Prespa Agreement, settling the Macedonia naming dispute.
Kyriakos Mitsotakis of New Democracy becomes prime minister; re-elected in June 2023 with 158 seats.

f.founder: Konstantinos Karamanlis, recalled from self-exile in 1974 to lead the return to democracy; the republican constitution of 1975 followed a referendum that chose not to restore the monarchy
f.predecessor: The Greek military junta of 1967–1974, and before it the Kingdom of Greece (abolished by referendum in 1974)
